scope: Preparation research review of the sealed v5 proposal only; not a product Actor, runtime-admission canary, or execution authorization.

reviewWindow.startBasis: The freeze timestamp is the earliest possible start; the exact reviewer dispatch timestamp was not exposed.

hashVerification.workingOnlyManifestEntry: evidence/study-input-bindings.json has no sealed Git blob id; its working bytes/hash are covered by the frozen manifest and raw archive hash.

findings.finding: The common profile is correctly NOT ADMITTED. The existing Design adapter's literal argv enables read-only sandboxing, ignores user configuration/rules, and disables plugins, shell_tool, and unified_exec. The collector treats observed tool-call items as tool use and returns incomplete; the adapter removes model-authored usage and attaches only collector events. Reusing that restricted workflow for strong Conventional would withhold its normal repository inspection/edit/build/test/debug/helper tools, while native full-tool use for Design has no established per-call provider input/output telemetry. No equivalent protected full-tool/telemetry path is evidenced, and weakening security or waiving the confound is not an acceptable inference from these pins.

The distinction between historical R12 receipts and actual true Verifier evidence is correct. R12 records 16 calls (6 work, 7 review, 3 integration) with historical token totals; those roles do not establish a true Verifier call. ProjectRun requires input and output usage to bound work, review, and any configured true Verifier cost, and verifier acceptance also requires coverage of required subjects/evidence. Generic optional usage or synthetic mapping cannot satisfy this.

The typed role and DTO claims are supported: Manager task/integration uses executor plus projectrun-task/v1 and TaskResponse; the independent Reviewer uses executor plus projectrun-review/v1 with candidate scope and a typed report, not the Manager transcript; true Verifier is a separate verifier role and request. Host response/coverage validation remains authoritative. The offline pass covers synthetic serialization/mapping only and explicitly did not run Host Go validators.

The Classic assessment is narrowly scoped and matches the copied selected-module source: markitect-dotnet both rejects extensions beyond .cs/.csproj and declares those extensions for its task. That supports incompatibility of this selected module/model/task with required JSON, lock, config, and docs; it does not establish a product-wide Markitect limitation.

The proposed actor-cap alternative is prospective, finite, and unallocated. It retains the original 7,200-second cell and 1,200-second task walls and 840-second implementation cutoff; the 144-cell/24-task activation caps are justified as capacity room by the historical 16-call flow, not as a universal Design minimum or evidence the six-stage task fits. Two follow-up slots stay unallocated. Attempt accounting, no refill, pair concurrency, setup/review costs, and the 300-second assessment minimum are stated. This is a proposal only, not a grant.

Staging retains the same public input hashes and private evaluation hashes only, unchanged declared requirements, an empty Greenfield tree, and the pinned Brownfield start. Task 5 is gated on its own actual Task 4 predecessor; Task 6 requires both paired Task 5 passes/freezes and separate equivalence review. No prebuilt solution/model or future/private evaluation content is included in the declared actor inputs. These are prospective bindings, not evidence that a cell ran or passed.

limitations: The candidate executable, Python, provider executable, adapter, source, and metadata digests are read pins; no claim is made that the pinned binaries were executed or that the serving model/account availability is currently known.
Historical R12 usage is preserved metadata evidence only. No new provider usage, serving model, or cost is known. The historical weighted accounting units are not price or economic evidence.
The single offline mechanical check passed in 0.0830383 seconds with synthetic-only inputs. It provides no product readiness, runtime equivalence, actual telemetry, or semantic/evaluation evidence.
Exact Brownfield predecessor and Task 6 equivalence are declared future gates; this review did not inspect prior cell outputs or private evaluator contents.
blockers: No admitted common, legitimately protected full-tool profile with equal actually available tool rights and real per-call input/output telemetry is established.

The native full-tool path does not establish ProjectRun-compatible provider-reported per-call input/output usage; the existing restricted adapter cannot be broadened without changing protections and refuses tool events.
No true Verifier usage receipt is evidenced by the 16 historical R12 roles or the synthetic check.
